security_problem: A stolen minted next-hop JWT is a bearer token at visor-gateway. Without proof-of-possession, theft of the compact JWS is enough to spoof --client-id until TTL or denylist. X-Forwarded-Proto must not become htu. DPoP jti must not be reusable. Private key material in the DPoP header jwk must be rejected.
required_behavior: Minted STS tokens include cnf.jkt of the actor-token verification key. visor-gateway requires a DPoP proof whose public JWK thumbprint equals cnf.jkt, with htm matching the method, htu reconstructed from this request (TLS, Host, path; no query/fragment; X-Forwarded-* ignored), ath matching SHA-256 of the access token, iat within clock skew, and jti consumed in -dpop-replay through iat+ClockSkew before allow. Missing cnf, missing DPoP, invalid proof, or replay is 401 with no backend. NewServer and the visor-gateway command require the replay cache.
failure_behavior: Fail closed: unreadable or aliased -dpop-replay, missing ProofReplay, and failed durable writes produce HTTP 503 or a process error and no backend forward.
